summary: U.S. equity markets closed higher Wednesday, with the S&P 500 rising 0.31% to 7,715 points as Treasury yields pulled back sharply following a surprise announcement from the U.S. Treasury Department. Officials said they plan to at least double buybacks of longer-dated government debt, targeting the 10- to 30-year maturities, aiming to ease borrowing costs after benchmark yields hit multi-decade highs. The 30-year Treasury yield plunged more than 10 basis points to 5.18%, while the dollar fell to a three-month low and gold climbed to its highest level since early June. In crypto markets, spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded their largest single-day inflow since early May—$517 million net—driven by the Treasury buyback news and a White House meeting with industry executives where President Trump pressed Congress to pass key crypto legislation. The SEC also proposed "Regulation Crypto Assets," a tailored framework offering exemptions and a safe harbor for digital asset startups, drawing praise from industry advocates. FOMC minutes released yesterday showed continued divisions over the Fed's next move, with three dissenters favoring a hike at the July meeting. Asian markets were set to rebound overnight, tracking Wall Street's gains and the weaker dollar.

signals.title: Treasury expands bond buyback program, yields plunge
signals.desc: U.S. Treasury will at least double buybacks of 10- to 30-year debt, driving 30-year yields down 10 bps to 5.18% and boosting rate-sensitive equities.

signals.title: FOMC minutes reveal hawkish dissent at July meeting
signals.desc: Three regional Fed presidents dissented in favor of a rate hike, the most since 2016, but majority sided with Chair Warsh to hold rates steady.

signals.title: Dollar hits 3-month low as yields collapse
signals.desc: DXY fell to its lowest level since mid-May as Treasury buyback news drove safe-haven outflows and supported commodities and risk assets.

verdict: Treasury's aggressive bond buyback and SEC crypto clarity create a risk-on backdrop, with ETF flows and falling yields supporting equities and digital assets into today's session.
